subject: community-medicine
title: Sub-Centre, PHC and CHC: Population Norms, Staffing and IPHS

steps.title: Population norms: the 5000-30000-120000 ladder
steps.tx: **Population norms** ladder upward: a sub-centre per 5000 population in plains (3000 in hilly, tribal, desert areas), a primary health centre per 30000 (20000 difficult), and a community health centre per 120000 (80000 difficult). Each CHC thus references about four PHCs and each PHC about six sub-centres, the arithmetic behind every infrastructure gap calculation.
steps.say: Five, thirty, one twenty thousand. Sub-centre, PHC, CHC, relaxed in hills and tribal belts. Four PHCs per CHC, six sub-centres per PHC: the arithmetic behind every gap calculation in examinations.

steps.title: Sub-centre: the ANM's outpost, now HWC
steps.tx: The **sub-centre** is the most peripheral fixed facility, staffed classically by ANM and male health worker pairs, delivering immunisation, antenatal, family planning and disease surveillance for its villages. Ayushman Bharat upgrades sub-centres into health and wellness centres (Ayushman Arogya Mandirs) led by community health officers delivering comprehensive primary care packages.
steps.say: The periphery lives here. ANM-led immunisation, antenatal and surveillance work for five thousand people, now upgrading into wellness centres under community health officers with comprehensive packages.

steps.title: PHC: first doctor, first referral
steps.tx: A **primary health centre** is the first contact with a medical officer, covering 30000 with curative OPD, maternal and child health, 24x7 delivery in upgraded facilities, minor surgery, and supervision of its sub-centres. Staffing norms add staff nurses, pharmacist, laboratory technician and health assistants to the medical officer core under Indian Public Health Standards.
steps.say: First doctor, first referral unit. Thirty thousand people, medical officer led, delivery capable when upgraded, supervising six sub-centres. Standards specify the nurse, pharmacist and technician around that core.

rows: OPD, maternal child health, minor procedures

steps.title: CHC: first referral unit with specialists
steps.tx: A **community health centre** serves 120000 as first referral unit with 30 beds and four specialist cores in IPHS design (medicine, surgery, obstetrics-gynaecology, paediatrics, with anaesthesia support), operation theatre, labour room, X-ray, laboratory and blood storage. Specialist vacancies against this norm are the chronic gap every health systems analysis quotes.
steps.say: Referral becomes real here. Thirty beds, four specialist cores, theatre, blood storage for one hundred twenty thousand. Vacant specialist posts against that norm are the chronic quoted gap.

nodes.label: PHC doctor gives first contact care

steps.title: IPHS: standards as entitlements
steps.tx: **Indian Public Health Standards** convert facilities from buildings into assured service packages: infrastructure, human resources, drugs, diagnostics and quality protocols per level, revised periodically (2022 revision aligning wellness centres). Gap analysis against IPHS, not against neighbouring districts, is the sanctioned planning method, and facility grading through quality frameworks operationalises it.
steps.say: Standards convert buildings into promises. Staff, drugs, diagnostics and protocols per level, gap analysis against the standard itself. Planning compares facilities with entitlements, not with neighbouring districts.

steps.title: Referral is a system, not a direction
steps.tx: **Referral discipline** fails when patients bypass levels (crowding district OPDs with sub-centre problems), transport is unarranged, or feedback never returns downward. Functioning referral needs communication before movement, transport (108 ambulances), stabilisation at origin, and counter-referral advice. Bypass rates therefore audit trust in lower levels, not patient indiscipline.
steps.say: Referral is logistics plus trust. Communication, transport, stabilisation, feedback downward. Bypassing audits lower-level trust, never patient character. Ambulance networks made the chain physical.

steps.title: Health and wellness centres: 12 packages
steps.tx: **Comprehensive primary care** at wellness centres expands beyond maternal-child work into 12 service packages: pregnancy and newborn, child and adolescent health, family planning, communicable and non-communicable disease management, mental health, eye, ENT, oral, elderly and palliative, emergency and trauma stabilisation. The expansion from selective to comprehensive is National Health Policy 2017's stated paradigm shift.
steps.say: Twelve packages replace selective care. Mental health, oral, eye, elderly, palliative and emergency stabilisation join the maternal-child core. Policy calls it the shift from selective to assured comprehensive primary care.

steps.title: Rogi Kalyan Samiti and untied funds
steps.tx: **Rogi Kalyan Samitis** (patient welfare committees) govern facilities with community representation, spending untied funds and annual maintenance grants on local gaps (cleanliness, minor repairs, patient amenities) without state sanction delays. Jan Arogya Samitis do the same at wellness centres. Decentralised small money, visibly spent, is the governance intervention behind many cleanliness transformations.
steps.say: Small local money, visibly governed. Facility committees with community members spend untied funds on cleanliness and repairs without distant sanctions. Decentralised rupees explain many transformed facilities.

steps.title: Staffing reality versus norms
steps.tx: **Vacancy analysis** separates sanctioned, posted and present: specialists at CHCs show the deepest shortfalls, while CHO deployment filled wellness centre leadership faster than doctor recruitment filled PHCs. Task-shifting (trained nurses and AYUSH practitioners in defined roles) and rural service bonds are the policy responses stems expect beside the vacancy numbers.
steps.say: Count three ways: sanctioned, posted, present. Specialist chairs empty deepest; wellness officers filled faster than PHC doctors. Task-shifting and service bonds are the quoted policy responses.
